chapter.title: The two bazaars and their price boards

cards.body: Our bazaar has two market buildings, *NSE* and *BSE*, with thousands of shops inside and the same inspector, SEBI, walking both floors. Above each door hangs a price board. **The board does not list every shop**: Nifty 50 shows one number for the 50 biggest shops in the NSE building, and Sensex shows one number for the 30 biggest in the BSE building.
cards.simpler: Think of the stock market as a bazaar with two big buildings, NSE and BSE. Each holds thousands of shops, and one inspector, SEBI, walks both floors. Over each door hangs a price board. **The board does not list every shop.** Nifty 50 gives one number for the 50 biggest shops in the NSE building. Sensex gives one number for the 30 biggest in the BSE building.

cards.prompt: You walk past the NSE building at 4 pm. The board reads 'Nifty 50: down 0.8%'. Your cousin says, 'so every company fell today.' What is the board actually telling you?

options.text: Every one of the 50 big shops dropped 0.8%
The 50 biggest shops, taken together, are worth 0.8% less than yesterday

whyNot.a: That's reading one average as 50 separate readings: the board is a combined number, and some of the 50 can rise on a day it falls.
whyNot.c: That's the whole bazaar, not the board: Nifty 50 tracks only 50 shops out of the thousands listed.

cards.reteach: Think of a cricket team's total. If the team scored fewer runs than last match, that does not mean every batter did worse. Nifty 50 is a team score for 50 companies, so one number can hide very different days for the players.

cards.title: Two buildings, one inspector
cards.body:
India has two stock exchanges, the *National Stock Exchange* (NSE) and the *Bombay Stock Exchange* (BSE), both based in Mumbai. Most large companies are listed in both, so the same share can be bought in either building at almost the same price.

Both open at 9:15 am and close at 3:30 pm, Monday to Friday, shut on market holidays. Outside those hours no trading happens, so a price you see at 8 pm is the 3:30 pm closing price.

**SEBI is the inspector for both.** The Securities and Exchange Board of India writes the rules, licenses brokers and punishes cheating. It does not set prices.
cards.simpler: India has two stock exchanges, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), both in Mumbai. Most big companies are listed on both, at almost the same price. Both open 9:15 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays and shut on market holidays. A price you see at 8 pm is the 3:30 pm closing price. **SEBI is the inspector for both.** It writes the rules, licenses brokers and punishes cheating, but does not set prices.

cards.title: Meera's bad headline
cards.body: Meera checks her phone on a made-up Tuesday: 'Nifty 50 closes 0.8% lower.' She owns 1 share of a bank that sits in the index, so she braces. Her bank is up 1.2%. On this invented day, 21 of the 50 rose and 29 fell, but the giants fell, and **the biggest shops pull the board hardest**. The headline was true. It just was not about her share.
cards.simpler: Meera checks her phone on a made-up Tuesday. The headline says Nifty 50 closed 0.8% lower. She owns one share of a bank that is in the index, so she expects bad news. But her bank is up 1.2%. On this invented day, 21 of the 50 companies rose and 29 fell. The giants fell, and **the biggest shops pull the board hardest**. The headline was true. It just was not about her share.

cards.prompt: It is 9 pm on a Wednesday. Your friend texts: 'Reliance just moved 2% on the BSE, check now!' Which reply is right?

options.text: Can't be. Both exchanges closed at 3:30 pm, so the last price is the 3:30 close.
BSE closes later than NSE, so it might be true.
SEBI must have approved an evening session for Reliance.

whyNot.b: That's mixing up the two buildings: NSE and BSE keep the same hours, 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.
whyNot.c: That's the inspector confused with the exchange: SEBI sets rules, it does not open the doors for one shop.

cards.reteach: Both market buildings keep the same hours, 9:15 am to 3:30 pm, Monday to Friday. Anything you see after 3:30 pm is the closing price, or news that will matter tomorrow. A price cannot move while the doors are shut.

cards.title: What the board weighs
cards.body:
The board is not a plain average. **Bigger shops pull the board harder.** Each company's share of the number depends on its size, measured by *market cap*, the price of one share times all the shares that exist. Chapter 5 goes deeper on that.

So a 2% fall in the largest company moves Nifty 50 far more than a 2% fall in the smallest of the 50. A 0.8% drop can mean three giants had a bad day while 30 others rose.

And the board says nothing at all about the thousands of smaller companies that are not in the 50 or the 30.
cards.simpler: The board is not a plain average. **Bigger shops pull the board harder.** Each company counts by its market cap, meaning one share's price times all its shares. So a 2% fall in the largest company moves Nifty 50 far more than the same fall in the smallest of the 50. A 0.8% drop can mean three giants had a bad day while 30 others rose. And it ignores the thousands of smaller companies outside the 50 or 30.

cards.body: Arjun sees 'Sensex at record high' and buys shares of a small textile company that afternoon, sure the whole bazaar is booming. His company is not one of the 30 on the Sensex board, and it drifts down 6% that week while the headline stays cheerful. Spot it: whenever a headline names Nifty or Sensex, **ask 'is my shop one of those 50 or 30?'** If not, the headline is about someone else's shelf.
cards.simpler: Arjun sees 'Sensex at record high' and buys shares of a small textile company that afternoon. He thinks the whole bazaar is booming. But his company is not one of the 30 on the Sensex board. It drifts down 6% that week while the headline stays cheerful. Spot it: whenever a headline names Nifty or Sensex, **ask 'is my shop one of those 50 or 30?'** If not, the headline is about someone else's shelf.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is the only one the price board can back up?

options.text: Sensex is up 1% today, so the 30 biggest BSE companies together gained about 1%.
Sensex is up 1% today, so every Indian company gained about 1%.
Sensex is up 1% today, so SEBI approved the market's rise.

whyNot.b: That's the whole bazaar, not the board: Sensex covers 30 companies out of thousands.
whyNot.c: That's the inspector mixed up with the price: SEBI polices honesty, it does not set or approve prices.

cards.reteach: A board is one combined number for a short list of the biggest shops. It tells you how that group did, with big shops counting more. It cannot tell you about any single company, or about shops outside the list.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: NSE and BSE are India's two exchanges, open 9:15 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays, with SEBI policing both. **Nifty 50 and Sensex are one-number scoreboards** for the 50 and 30 biggest companies, with big ones counting more, so a board moving tells you about the group, not about any one share.
cards.simpler: NSE and BSE are India's two stock exchanges. They open 9:15 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays, and SEBI polices both. **Nifty 50 and Sensex are one-number scoreboards** for the 50 and 30 biggest companies. Big companies count more. So when a board moves, it tells you about the group, not about any one share.

cards.body: Tonight, search 'Nifty 50 today' or open any finance app. Note the % change. Then look up one Nifty 50 company you have heard of. Did it move the same way as the board?
cards.simpler: Tonight, search 'Nifty 50 today' or open any finance app. Write down the % change, up or down. Then pick one Nifty 50 company you have heard of and look up its price change for the same day. **Did it move the same way as the board?** If not, you have just seen for yourself that the board is about the group, not any one share.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now read 'Nifty closed 0.8% down' and say what it does and does not tell you about the 50 companies behind it.
